messages:
rachel: seeing a cluster of incidents created in the last 10m but PD escalations didn't fire for several of them. Is anyone else seeing suppressed pages?

devon: yea I just noticed, some incidents show as `resolved` in the console but we never got pages. looks like notify-orchestrator generated the incident but the escalation pipeline stopped at the broker.

oncall-bot: [automated] incident created: notify-orchestrator:error-rate-high (id: io-5321) — severity: P2 — created at 2612347820

rachel: thanks bot. @ops-sre can you check PD outbound logs? maybe webhooks are being 429'd.

ops-sre: looking now. initial check: PD accepted webhooks but our broker ack queue length is growing. suspect a backpressure bug in the orchestration worker. grabbing tail of logs.

ops-sre: log snippet:
```
2026-03-17T12:11:05Z broker: enqueue event id=io-5321 route=escalation pipeline=null
2026-03-17T12:11:06Z broker: dispatch failed id=io-5321 err=ack-timeout attempts=1
2026-03-17T12:11:07Z worker: retry-loop backoff=500ms queue-depth=812
2026-03-17T12:11:10Z worker: starved routes: [noncritical-escalation] high-prio-blocking=true
```

sam: queue-depth 800+ seems bad. any recent deploy to the broker or rate-limiter?

devon: we rolled a config change to the notify-limiter yesterday that changed token-bucket weights; might be starving lower-prio routes. rolling that back is low-risk.

rachel: manual mitigation: can someone flip `notify-limiter.weights` back to previous value and restart the broker worker? I'll start manual paging for any P1/P2 until automated pages are healthy.

ops-sre: doing rollback now. applying config v2026-03-16-1145 -> `kubectl apply -f notify-limiter-weights.yaml` then restart deployment notify-broker.

ops-sre: restart command used:
```
kubectl rollout restart deploy/notify-broker -n infra || true
```

ops-sre: restarted. queue depth dropping: 812 -> 120 -> 42. PD webhooks for stalled incidents are now being resent.

pagerduty-bot: [automated] webhook retry succeeded for incident io-5321, escalation triggered to oncall team SRE-Platform.

sam: confirm: did any customers receive delayed notifications or degraded UX? Need to scope impact for the postmortem.

rachel: initial check: handful of customers (mostly smaller dev org tenants) reported slower alert-to-ack times; no customer-visible downtime. marking impact as "delayed paging" for 6 customers.

devon: root cause suspect: token-bucket weight change caused starvation of lower-priority escalation routes under burst traffic, combined with worker backoff that magnified queue growth. We'll add a guard to fail-open on weight misconfig and add queue-depth alarm in CloudWatch.

rachel: good. action items: 1) ops-sre - add queue-depth alert at 200 and paging-failure alert at 5m; 2) devon - PR to add fail-open and unit test for notify-limiter weights; 3) sam - customer comms draft for affected tenants. I'll start manual page audit for last 30m and file a postmortem.

ops-sre: working on alerts now.

sam: drafting comms, will post to #support-review in 15m.

rachel: thanks team. once the postmortem is open I'll link to this thread. :white_check_mark:
